chapter: Theater broadcasts, recordings and the road
title: Vaudeville tour with Adelaide Hughes and pasting orchestrations together
summary: He describes joining a vaudeville act as a trumpet feature, improvising by combining stock orchestrations, and playing next to Eisenhower.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: No. We had another fellow from the Russian Symphony, Eisenhower. He played lead trumpet and I played hop trumpet. But I will say that I created more attention than he did because I get up and take a chorus and it was absolutely strange to their ears. I toured the, they offered the theater clothes with an act called Adelaide Hughes. I don't know whether you remember that. They were two of the greatest dancers that ever lived. She was known as La Petite Adelaide. He danced on her toes. And Jimmy Hughes was an athletic sort of a dancer. He did an Indian dance and I swear he leaped the queen across the stage. So their violinist was drafted. They had no leader. But they had a spot in their show where they had to have something happen because it was a two act and they had to change their clothes for the finale. And Mr. Tasso played a miserable violin. He directed well, but when he tried to play something it wouldn't do to kill the spot. So they heard me playing down in the pit and they came to me and said, will you go with us on the interstate second? I said, well I'll talk to my wife. She said, how long is it? She said, it's six weeks. And she said, never one of those unnecessary jobs, you know what I mean? But she wouldn't, she knew I was ambitious, she knew how musicians were so. She said, we want you for one reason. In the middle of our act, as you know, instead of the violinist, we want you to fill that spot. I said, I can do it. It's probably me anyway. So I made a, I grabbed a hold of two stock orchestrations. One was the sunshine of your smile. You remember that?

And I, I hooked that onto the storybook ball for no reason whatsoever except that I had an orchestration that I could waste all the storybook ball. I would paste them up. And then I hadn't reached that stage where I had the radius done. So I pasted them together and wrote in a modulation. And I'd stand up and, wait.
And attached to it was the chorus of some of these days.
